# isBoolean

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a boolean.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isBoolean() — Checks whether a value is a boolean. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isBoolean(value: unknown): value is boolean;
```

Only the two primitives pass. `new Boolean(false)` is an object, and the strings `"true"` and `"false"` are strings.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a boolean; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `boolean` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isBoolean(true); // => true
isBoolean(false); // => true
isBoolean("true"); // => false
isBoolean(1); // => false
isBoolean(null); // => false
```
